_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 4 Mathematics unit lecture film, Lesson 3 Ways to Calculate. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow the lesson page's own steps in order - Estimate before you work (387 + 214), Adding it exactly (347 + 185), Taking away exactly (623 - 187), Tables and a shortcut with the lecture's own 225 + 98, Multiplying a big number (342 x 6) and Sharing out (87 / 5), and 6s 7s 9s and factor pairs (24) - in the lesson's own numbers. Every sum the pictures draw is ART.columnSum's own computed working, so the carries and exchanges cannot disagree with the digits above them.
title: Ways to Calculate
subtitle: Grade 4 Mathematics
objectives: Estimate, add and subtract whole numbers with up to three digits.
Understand the associative property of multiplication, and use this to simplify calculations.
Estimate and multiply whole numbers up to 1000 by 1-digit whole numbers.
Estimate and divide whole numbers up to 100 by 1-digit whole numbers.
Understand the relationship between multiples and factors.

beats.say: Maths gives you more than one way to work something out.
Estimate first, then choose the method that fits the numbers.
Here is a sum to work out. What is 387 add 214?
Before you calculate, round each number to something easy.
387 is nearly 400, and 214 is a little past 200.
400 add 200 is 600, so the answer should be about 600.
An estimate is not the answer. It shows when one looks silly.
Now work one out exactly. Line the digits up in their own columns.
Take 347 add 185. Start at the ones: 7 and 5 make 12.
Write the 2 down, and carry the ten into the tens column.
The tens are 4, 8 and the carried ten, which together make 13.
Write 3 and carry a hundred. The hundreds make 5, so the answer is 532.
Taking away needs the opposite of carrying. Try 623 take away 187.
3 is less than 7, so exchange a ten. Now 13 take away 7 is 6.
The tens now hold 1, so exchange a hundred. 11 take away 8 is 3.
Then 5 take away 1 is 4, and the answer is 436.
Look at 225 add 98. Some sums are quicker without columns.
98 is nearly 100. Add 100 instead, and you get 325.
You added 2 too many, so take those 2 away again. That leaves 323.
Work out 4 times 7 times 5. Multiplying can be regrouped too.
4 times 5 is 20, and 20 times 7 is 140. Much easier that way.
Try 342 times 6. To multiply a big number, break it into parts.
342 splits into 300, 40 and 2. Multiply each part on its own.
300 times 6 is 1,800. 40 times 6 is 240. 2 times 6 is 12.
Add the three parts back, and you get 2,052. Miss one and you are short.
What is 87 divided by 5? Dividing keeps taking whole groups away.
17 fives make 85, and 2 are left over. So it is 17 remainder 2.
Lay 24 counters out as a rectangle: 4 rows of 6.
4 and 6 multiply to make 24, so they are a factor pair.
24 has more pairs: 1 and 24, 2 and 12, and 3 and 8.
Do not stop at the first pair. Keep going until they repeat.
One fact, two names. 4 is a factor of 24, and 24 is a multiple of 4.
Estimate first, then work it out exactly in columns.
Or take a shortcut: give 2 back, or regroup a multiplication.
Split a big number, share into fives, and look for factor pairs.
